value: building-gnustep-app-target-on-macos: Creating a GNUstep application.make target on macOS requires several non-obvious steps beyond the basic makefile variables. (1) Use per-target NEEDS_GUI variables (AppName_NEEDS_GUI = yes/no) rather than a global NEEDS_GUI. (2) Use RESOURCE_FILES_DIR + wildcard to copy script/resource files directly into Resources/ top level — RESOURCE_DIRS only creates empty directories; RESOURCE_FILES with a path creates a subdirectory; NSBundle URLsForResourcesWithExtension:subdirectory:nil only searches Resources/ top level and language subdirectories, not arbitrary subdirs. (3) Set MAIN_MODEL_FILE = MainMenu.nib to populate NSMainNibFile in Info.plist; compile the xib with ibtool in an after-AppName-all:: double-colon target (guard with xcrun --find ibtool so it skips on Linux). (4) Embed built frameworks in Contents/Frameworks/ via cp -Rf in after-all, then use install_name_tool -change to rewrite the relative framework install name to @executable_path/../Frameworks/...; add -Wl,-headerpad_max_install_names to LDFLAGS so install_name_tool has room to write longer paths. (5) Also rewrite libgnustep-baseadd's bare install name to its full /usr/local/lib/ path the same way. (6) Re-sign the binary with 'codesign --sign - --force' after all install_name_tool changes (omit --preserve-metadata=entitlements as it fails on unsigned binaries). Without re-signing, Apple Silicon will refuse to run the modified binary.

GNUstep Make reserves several top-level phony targets using double-colon rules (e.g. check::, install::, clean::) defined in $(GNUSTEP_MAKEFILES)/Master/rules.make. Custom GNUmakefiles must NOT redefine these with single-colon rules (causes 'has both : and :: entries' error). Instead, hook into the corresponding double-colon extension points: before-<target>::, internal-<target>::, or after-<target>::. Example: to add custom logic to 'make check', define 'internal-check::' rather than 'check:'. Discovered while implementing appscript-z0t. Worth writing up as generic GNUstep Make documentation for reuse across projects and by other agents.
